core_claims.name: Eval / evalValue / evalDeterministic
core_claims.scope: Substitution-based weak call-by-name semantics for every scope. Every finite successful derivation returns a lambda, and two derivations for the same input return the identical term. No universal convergence assertion.

core_claims.name: HeadStep / HeadSteps / headDeterministic / headIsBeta / headsAreBetas
core_claims.scope: Deterministic weak call-by-name small steps and paths, with a proved inclusion into unrestricted full beta steps and paths.

core_claims.name: evalToHeadSteps / headExpand / headStepsToEval / evalToSteps
core_claims.scope: Constructive equivalence between Eval to a specified lambda and weak head-step reachability of that lambda, plus the forward inclusion into full beta reachability.

core_claims.name: Closure / Env / ClosEval / closDeterministic
core_claims.scope: Finite closure/environment trees and genuine lazy closure call-by-name evaluation. The argument retains its call-site environment and is not evaluated when stored. Successful closure results are unique.

core_claims.name: reify / reifyEnv / reifyBeta / closToEval / closToSteps / closedClosToLambda
core_claims.scope: Total reification of arbitrary closures into closed syntax, environment-extension/substitution correspondence, and conversion of every closure evaluation into substitution evaluation and full beta paths. A closed successful closure run yields a beta path to a lambda.

core_claims.name: BoundedEval / weakenBound / evalBound / forgetBound
core_claims.scope: A proof-height annotation on existing finite evaluation derivations. Every Eval derivation has some constructively produced bound; forgetting the bound recovers Eval. The bound is not a fixed restriction on the language.

core_claims.name: ClosureValue / closValue / boundedToClos / evalToClos / closedEvalToClos
core_claims.scope: Reverse correspondence for every closure: Eval (reify input) value constructs a result closure, actual ClosEval input result evidence, and reify result = value. Mutual recursion decreases derivation bound or closure/environment structure. Closed-term specialization restores the bridge used by upstream closure-valued adequacy.

core_claims.name: run / RunResult / headView
core_claims.scope: Total fuel evaluator for the weak strategy. Returned, Blocked and OutOfFuel all contain certified HeadSteps traces. Open neutral heads may contain arbitrary arguments; exhaustion does not prove divergence.

core_claims.name: omegaNoEval / ignoreOmegaTerminates / lazyCaptureTerminates / closureLazyCapture
core_claims.scope: No finite weak Eval derivation exists for Omega, proved by recursion on the alleged derivation. Ignoring Omega and returning a lambda that captures Omega both have checked evaluations; the second also has an actual closure evaluation.

deviations: Closures use finite indexed list environments instead of functions from finite contexts. Both terms and their saved environments remain lazy.

A substitution-based presentation and its matching weak small-step relation are added before the closure presentation. Bidirectional reification theorems prove the connection; closure-valued adequacy is retained in Part3.

The reverse correspondence is split into ClosureBounds and ClosureCorrespondence for acyclic imports. Its natural-number bound is extracted from each supplied finite Eval derivation and is not a theorem restriction.
The total executable weak evaluator returns traces and distinguishes open neutrals from exhausted fuel; no fuel result is used alone as a divergence proof.
